newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ says profit outlook unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ says profit outlook unchanged.

text.p: Major Czech electricity producer CEZ a.s. said on Thursday it was not changing its 1996 profit forecast after the Finance Ministry set its 1996 supply prices retroactively at an average of 0.2 percent above 1995.
Earlier on Thursday, the Finance Ministry set the average price for 1996 at 1,035 crowns/Mwh after 1,033 in 1995.

CEZ spokesman Miroslav Novak told Reuters that CEZ had not changed its 8.0 billion crown net profit forecast, according to Czech accounting standards, though it had been hopeful that the average price would be set at around 1,040 crowns per Mwh.

"The price is a little higher than last year's, a little lower than we negotiated for. But thanks to higher energy consumption...in no case should we have a worse result than planned," Novak said adding that the consumption was rising six percent, year on year.
CEZ had been locked in a lenghty row with the country's eight regional power distributors over the prices, and was charging provisional bills since the beginning of the year.
It said that the situation was the main factor which bit into its first half result, which declined 8.5 percent compared with the same period of 1995 to 5.1 billion crowns, under Czech accounting.
Under international accounting standards, the first half net profit was down 4.9 percent year on year to 5.95 billion crowns. CEZ has said it would pay out first-ever dividends on 1996 earnings.

Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said earlier this week that an agreement has been reached on an algorythm that should be used for price calculations in the following years as well, preventing stop-gap situations.
